title: Kernel auto-selection v2 (umbrella): table-driven kernel selector + telemetry + rollout
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Summary
Kernel auto-selection v2 is a Serving Runtime Performance initiative to ship improved GPU kernel selection logic that chooses the best attention/prefill/decode kernels based on:
1) **Model family** (architecture + flags like GQA/MQA)
2) **Effective sequence length buckets** (prefill vs decode regimes)
3) **GPU SKU/capability** (L4, A10, A100, H100; SM capability + MIG/partition nuances)

This is an umbrella issue tracking scope, success metrics, milestones, rollout, and links.

## Why
We currently see avoidable variance in tail latency across GPUs and prompt distributions due to heuristic-heavy selection and implicit behavior. Kernel selector v2 makes selection **explicit, deterministic, and data-driven** to reduce regressions as we onboard new model families and new GPU generations.

## Goals
- Improve **p95 latency** and **cost/token** for mixed workloads by selecting kernels that match regime (short vs long context; prefill vs decode).
- Reduce tail-latency variance across GPU SKUs by using explicit selection tables + normalized GPU capability detection.
- Provide safe rollout controls:
  - feature-flagged v2 selector
  - deterministic fallback to v1 selector
  - per-model-family overrides + emergency kill switch
- Improve observability:
  - record selection decision (selector version, kernel id, model family, seq bucket, GPU)
  - correlate with latency/correctness signals
- Expand regression prevention:
  - perf-canary gates
  - benchmark-lab coverage across representative prompt distributions

## Non-goals
- Writing new kernels from scratch (this is selection + integration).
- Changing customer-facing API semantics.
- Large scheduler redesign (only minimal wiring needed to expose seq regime + batching context).

## Deliverables
- Table-driven kernel selector v2 implementation (gated by config + feature flag) in runtime.
- Kernel registry schema + versioning, including model-family identifiers and seq-length buckets.
- Telemetry/events/metrics for selection decisions + trace annotations with cardinality controls.
- Perf suite + canary gates updated; benchmark reports comparing v1 vs v2.
- Operator runbook for overrides/rollbacks; release notes for runtime version.

## Success metrics (initial acceptance thresholds)
**Primary**
- Hosted: for mixed prompt distributions, v2 improves or matches v1 with:
  - **p95 latency:** >= 5% improvement overall, and no GPU SKU worse than **+2%** p95 relative regression at steady state.
  - **throughput (tok/s):** >= 3% improvement on at least 2/4 primary SKUs (L4/A10/A100/H100) with no sustained regressions.

**Secondary**
- Reduced variance: p95 spread across L4/A10/A100/H100 decreases for representative long-context buckets.
- Observability: selection decision visible in traces and aggregated metrics with bounded cardinality.
- Safety: unknown model family never crashes; defaults to safe kernel set and/or v1 fallback.

**Correctness gate**
- Conformance tests pass across representative shapes/seq buckets; NaN/overflow checks added for known-risk kernels.

## Milestones (tracking)
- Phase 0: baseline data + model-family taxonomy + registry schema
- Phase 1: selector v2 implementation + telemetry + runtime/scheduler wiring
- Phase 2: benchmark matrix + perf-canary gate + conformance tests
- Phase 3: staged rollout (internal -> 5% hosted -> 25% hosted -> dedicated opt-in -> default-on) + docs

## Rollout plan (high level)
- Default selector remains v1; v2 is enabled per-tier/region by feature flag.
- Rollback path must be < 5 minutes to global disable in Hosted.
- Dedicated: opt-in first, with per-cluster override support; provide guidance to CS/Support.

## Risks / watchouts
- Correctness: wrong kernel selection can cause silent numerical issues (NaNs) or shape mismatches.
  - Mitigation: conformance tests + safe kernel set + fallback to v1.
- Observability cardinality: selection telemetry can explode label space.
  - Mitigation: GPU/model bucketing; sampling; adhere to telemetry standards.
- Determinism: selection must be stable for identical inputs.
  - Mitigation: explicit tie-breaking and canonicalized context fields.
- Backward compatibility: missing/partial model metadata must not break serving.
  - Mitigation: unknown-family behavior defined; conservative fallback.

## Current status (as of 2026-02-22)
- Selector v2 core landed behind flag; unknown-family fallback hotfix merged.
- Seq-length bucketing wired from scheduler; off-by-one boundary bug fixed in follow-up.
- Telemetry label set reduced after initial cardinality review.
- Next: complete benchmark sweep across full GPU/model matrix; finalize perf-canary thresholds; prepare 5% Hosted canary (us-east) with SRE sign-off.

## Notes for triage / support
If we see suspected selector-induced regressions or NaNs:
- Immediately disable selector v2 via kill switch (Hosted) or override (Dedicated).
- Capture selector decision context (selector_version, kernel_id, model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_bucket) from traces.
- File follow-up under ENG-3928 (correctness) and ENG-3933 (dashboards/alerts) as appropriate.
